item.title: - Bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who are endowed with virtue, endowed with concentration, endowed with wisdom, endowed with liberation, endowed with knowledge and vision of liberation…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who are endowed with virtue, endowed with concentration, endowed with wisdom, endowed with liberation, endowed with knowledge and vision of liberation — I say that seeing those bhikkhus brings great benefit. Hearing those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, I say brings great benefit. Paying homage to those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, I say brings great benefit. Associating with those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, I say brings great benefit. Remembering those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, I say brings great benefit. Following those bhikkhus into homelessness, bhikkhus, I say brings great benefit. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, when hearing the Dhamma from such bhikkhus, one lives in seclusion, with two kinds of seclusion: seclusion of body and seclusion of mind. One who lives in seclusion thus will recollect that Dhamma and reflect on that Dhamma.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 46.3

item.title: Whatever beings, bhikkhus, in the morning do good bodily actions, good verbal actions, good mental actions — those beings, bhikkhus, have a good morning. Whatever…
item.description:
Whatever beings, bhikkhus, in the morning do good bodily actions, good verbal actions, good mental actions — those beings, bhikkhus, have a good morning. Whatever beings, bhikkhus, at noon do good bodily actions, good verbal actions, good mental actions — those beings, bhikkhus, have a good noon. Whatever beings, bhikkhus, in the evening do good bodily actions, good verbal actions, good mental actions — those beings, bhikkhus, have a good evening.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.155

item.title: One who has seen the supreme, And heard the unsurpassed, Gained the unsurpassed, Delights in the unsurpassed training, Established in service, Develops the specific recollections,…
item.description:
One who has seen the supreme,
And heard the unsurpassed,
Gained the unsurpassed,
Delights in the unsurpassed training,
Established in service,
Develops the specific recollections,
Connected to seclusion,
Attains security, the Deathless,
Joyful, not heedless,
Careful, guarding virtue,
When the time has ripened,
Suffering is destroyed.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.30

item.title: - Just as a great crowd of people, bhikkhus, would gather together and say: 'The national beauty! The national beauty!' And that national beauty, with…
item.description:
- Just as a great crowd of people, bhikkhus, would gather together and say: 'The national beauty! The national beauty!' And that national beauty, with all her charms, would dance for them, with all her charms, would sing for them. And an even larger crowd would gather and say: 'The national beauty dances and sings.' Then a man would come who wants to live, not to die, who wants happiness and loathes suffering. They would say to him: 'Friend, look here. This is a bowl filled with oil. You must carry this bowl of oil through the great crowd and the national beauty. And a man with a drawn sword will follow behind you. Wherever you spill even a little of the oil, there your head will fall.' What do you think, bhikkhus, would that man, not attending to the bowl of oil, let his mind wander outside?" - "Bhikkhus, I give this simile to convey the meaning. And this is the meaning: 'The bowl filled with oil' is a synonym for mindfulness of the body. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: 'We will develop mindfulness of the body, cultivate it, make it our vehicle, make it our base, establish it, accumulate it, and properly undertake it.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 47.20

item.title: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in hell. What five? Stinginess regarding dwellings, stinginess regarding families,…
item.description:
Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in hell. What five? Stinginess regarding dwellings, stinginess regarding families, stinginess regarding gains, stinginess regarding praise, and causing donated goods to be wasted. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in hell. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in heaven. What five? No stinginess regarding dwellings, no stinginess regarding families, no stinginess regarding gains, no stinginess regarding praise, and not causing donated goods to be wasted. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu residing in a place is, as such, placed in heaven.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.239

item.title: - Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending. This is my instruction to you. And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu mindful? Here, bhikkhus,…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending. This is my instruction to you. And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu mindful? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world ... Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu mindful. And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu clearly comprehending? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu knows feelings as they arise, knows feelings as they persist, knows feelings as they pass away; knows perceptions as they arise, knows perceptions as they persist, knows perceptions as they pass away. Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu clearly comprehending. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending. This is my instruction to you.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 47.35

item.title: Bhikkhus, if one does not intend, does not plan, but still has a tendency towards something, that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness.…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, if one does not intend, does not plan, but still has a tendency towards something, that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a basis, there is a support for the establishment of consciousness. When consciousness is established and grows, there is the production of future renewed existence. When there is future renewed existence, future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the origination of this whole mass of suffering.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.38

item.title: - What gives birth to a person? What always runs? What undergoes rebirth? Because of what is there no liberation? - Craving gives birth to…
item.description:
- What gives birth to a person?
What always runs?
What undergoes rebirth?
Because of what is there no liberation?
- Craving gives birth to a person,
The mind always runs,
Beings undergo rebirth,
Because of suffering, there is no liberation.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.56

item.title: And, bhikkhus, when that bhikkhu has dwelt in these five things, four more things should be developed. The perception of foulness should be developed to…
item.description:
And, bhikkhus, when that bhikkhu has dwelt in these five things, four more things should be developed. The perception of foulness should be developed to abandon greed; loving-kindness should be developed to abandon hatred; mindfulness of breathing should be developed to cut off thoughts; the perception of impermanence should be developed to uproot conceit. Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu with the perception of impermanence, the perception of non-self becomes established; for a bhikkhu with the perception of non-self, conceit is uprooted, and in this very life he attains Nibbāna.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.1

item.title: For one who has no 'I' and 'mine' in regard to name-and-form, Who does not grieve over what is not, That one is truly called…
item.description:
For one who has no 'I' and 'mine' in regard to name-and-form,
Who does not grieve over what is not,
That one is truly called a bhikkhu.

A bhikkhu who dwells in loving-kindness,
With faith in the Buddha's teaching,
Attains the peaceful state,
The blissful state of peace.

Bhikkhu, empty this boat;
Empty, it will go quickly.
Having cut off greed and hatred,
You will go to Nibbāna.

From: Dhammapada 360-382
